issues.reason: Coordination & plurals states that coordinated noun phrases are distributive by default ("replicate the whole predication once per conjunct", "many events = distributive; one event with many agents = collective") and licenses the one-event form only for reciprocal/aggregate predicates or bare "together / jointly / between them", none of which "defeat" has, so the two Theme atoms on one (sk_defeat $x) are the unlicensed collective shape.

gaps_confirmed: comma-set participial adjunct on the subject read as a conditional restriction ("Power, wrongly used, defeats …"): the reduced-relative rule covers attributive participles on a noun, but not this adverbial/conditional use nor its promotion into a rule premise

"as well as" as an additive coordinator: the coordination rules specify plain "X and Y" only, and the additive contribution has no carrier here (the Also focus particle is specified for adverbial "as well", not for the coordinator)
new_gaps: distributing a coordinated NP inside a rule conclusion: the Skolem-function convention is (sk_<verb> $x), and nothing states how to name the two distinct per-binding events the distributive default requires (the flat case uses sk_leave_1 / sk_leave_2)
repair_summary: Split the single (sk_defeat $x) event carrying two Theme atoms into two per-binding events (sk_defeat_1 $x) and (sk_defeat_2 $x), each with its own Member/Agent atoms and one Theme (oppressor, oppressed), per the distributive default; premise, quantifier-free rule shape, proof name and TV untouched.
notes: The rule routing, the reduced-relative use event in the premise, surface-form (Manner … wrongly), Agent on the inanimate transitive subject and the 0.9/0.9 empirical generic TV all stand. Dropping the additive force of "as well as" is droppage in gap territory, not a falsehood, so it warranted no repair.
